title: OrbitLab Body-Expansion Discovery
scope: Read-only discovery to expand OrbitLab's supported central bodies (Mercury, Venus, Earth, Moon/Luna, Mars, Jupiter, Sun) and enable heliocentric orbits. Discovery artifact only: inventories assumptions, records GMAT facts verified by actually running NASA GMAT R2026a, proposes a design (not implemented), and performs physics sanity checks.
status: Discovery only. No production code changed. No network. No new dependencies. No training. All runtime scratch/output kept outside the repo (in the approved Temp directory); the in-repo body_expansion\ folder contains only this .json and sibling body_expansion_discovery.md.
evidence_rules: Every factual claim cites a repo file:line, a path into the installed GMAT R2026a (C:\Users\canit\XY\Downloads\gmat-win-R2026a), or captured command output. Items not verified are flagged UNVERIFIED with the exact verification procedure. No values invented.
unverified_summary: Mercury GM, Earth GM, Luna GM, Mars GM convention

gmat_install.invocation: GmatConsole.exe --run <script.script> --exit (executed from the bin working directory)

task_a_inventory.summary: OrbitLab supports exactly three central bodies today: Earth, Moon, Mars. Every place constraining or assuming a body is enumerated below. All body assumptions anywhere in the codebase are one of Earth, Moon, Mars.

a1_physical_constants.what: BODY_COORD_SYSTEM = {Earth: EarthMJ2000Eq, Moon: LunaMJ2000Eq, Mars: MarsMJ2000Eq}
CENTRAL_BODY_PROPERTIES maps only Earth/Moon/Mars to (radius, mu, gmat_body, coord_system)

a2_type_schema_constraints.what: centralBody: Literal["Earth","Moon","Mars"] (Pydantic literal; rejects any other body)
pointMasses: List[Literal["Luna","Sun","Jupiter"]] (perturber list already allows Luna/Sun/Jupiter but not as central bodies)
validator maps body -> coordinate system only for Earth/Moon/Mars

a3_gmat_script_generation.what: derives central_body, radius/mu; creates body-centered CoordinateSystem only for non-Earth bodies; GM mapping via CENTRAL_BODY_PROPERTIES
ForceModel.CentralBody, PrimaryBodies={gmat_body}, sets GravityField.<body>.Degree/Order; special-cases PotentialFile only for Mars (Mars50c.cof) and Moon (LP165P.cof)

b1_ephemeris_source.note: Every successful run printed 'Successfully set Planetary Source to use: DE405' and 'Kernel .../data/planetary_ephem/spk/DE405AllPlanets.bsp has been loaded.'
b1_ephemeris_source.nuance: bin\gmat_startup_file.txt:118 lists PLANETARY_SPK_FILE = .../DE421AllPlanets.bsp but the runtime loaded and used DE405AllPlanets.bsp per the console log. Body GM/radius/constants from DE405 are cited to data\planetary_ephem\spk\Readme-DE405AllPlanets.txt.

b2_radii_all_seven_bodies.note: Equatorial/mean radii in km (NAIF triplet = x, y, z). This TPC kernel contains no GM values (verified: no BODYxxx_GM entries).

task_b_gmat_facts.b3_unverified_gm: Mercury GM, Earth GM, Luna GM are UNVERIFIED from shipped files (see b6).

b4_set_only_properties.execution_proof: A GMAT script that tried 'y = Mercury.Mu' and 'ReportFile.Add = {Mercury.Mu}' both failed with '... is not a valid Parameter Type' / 'Undefined function, object, or disallowed object field'. Therefore GMAT body Mu/EquatorialRadius cannot be read back through a script; any GMAT-verified numeric GM for Mercury/Earth/Luna is not obtainable via script and must come from an external authoritative source.

venus_centered.configuration: VenusMJ2000Eq CS with Origin=Venus; SMA=7000, ECC=0, INC=90; RungeKutta89; 1800 s. Force model FMVenus: CentralBody=Venus, PrimaryBodies={Venus}, GravityField.Venus.Degree/Order=4 (uses default MGNP180U.cof; log line 'Using default potential file .../MGNP180U.cof for GravityField object GravityField.Venus').
venus_centered.result: Mission run completed ... successful. Telemetry: SMA held 6999.9-7000.0 km over the arc, ECC <= ~1.1e-5, VZ(t=0)=6.81236899 km/s. PASS.

sun_centered.configuration: SunMJ2000Eq CS with Origin=Sun; SMA=149597870.7 (1 AU), ECC=0; 1800 s. Force model models Sun as a point mass: CentralBody=Sun, PrimaryBodies={}, PointMasses={Sun}, no GravityField.Sun degree/order.
sun_centered.result: Mission run completed ... successful. Telemetry: SMA held 149597870.7 km, ECC <= ~7.7e-16, VY(t=0)=29.78464647 km/s. PASS.

b5_1_sun_negative_result.finding: Sun cannot be a harmonic primary.
b5_1_sun_negative_result.failure: First attempt set FMSun.GravityField.Sun.Degree/Order and/or PrimaryBodies={Sun} and failed: 'ODEModel Exception Thrown: There is no gravity file specified for GravityField GravityField.Sun' / '*** Mission run failed. (exit code 1)'.
b5_1_sun_negative_result.cause: From docs\help\html\ForceModel.html:236-247: bodies in PrimaryBodies use the potential file's constants in the equations of motion, and no Sun potential file is shipped; bodies in PointMasses use the body's Mu. Verified: data\gravity\other (Sun/Mercury/Jupiter location) is empty. GMAT ships harmonic-coefficient potential files only for Earth/Moon/Mars/Venus; Sun, Mercury, and Jupiter can only be modeled as point masses with this installation.

b6_why_script_cannot_yield_gm: No Mercury potential file ships (data\gravity\other empty).

Earth/Luna potential files ship but their GM lives inside the .cof binary header rather than as a script-readable value; the same set-only block prevents reading the body's Mu. Earth/Luna GM available only from external references, not GMAT script output, on this install.

b7_reportfile_add.note: ReportFile.Add = {a, b, c}; must be on a SINGLE line (multi-line fails); see docs\help\html\ReportFile.html:19 and :118. Reference generator emits a one-line Add (generator.py:259-266).

b8_reportfile_path.note: ReportFile.Filename must be an absolute path (or the process working directory must be where you want the file). A relative 'venus_telemetry.txt' produced no file; switching to an absolute path produced the telemetry on the next run. Reference generator always passes an absolute path (tests/test_gmat_execution.py:85,90; generator.py:256).

b9_integrators.note: RungeKutta89 is valid; RungeKutta8 is NOT (fails). Reference: tests/test_gmat_execution.py:78.

task_c_design_proposal.mars_mu_discrepancy: Codebase uses 42828.375214 (constants.py:14, build_v9.py:51) while GMAT's Mars50c.cof header GM is 42828.370371 - a 4.8e-6 relative difference. Proposed table uses the GMAT Mars50c value for GMAT consistency and flags the operationally-used value.

c2_proposed_code_changes.change: Extend CENTRAL_BODY_PROPERTIES to all seven bodies with the C.1 table (resolve UNVERIFIED mu first).
Widen centralBody literal, the coordinate-system literal, and the body->CS validator; keep pointMasses literal (187-190) but allow bodies as central.

Generalize CS creation and ForceModel generation: Venus keeps default potential (already works); Sun/Mercury/Jupiter emit point-mass-only force model per B.5.1 (CentralBody=<body>, PrimaryBodies={}, PointMasses={<body>}) and do NOT emit GravityField.<body>.Degree/Order when no potential file exists; always emit an absolute ReportFile.Filename (B.8).
Extend BODY_RADII_KM, BODY_COORD_SYSTEM, and per-body MIN_ALT guards.
Extend BODY and MIN_ALT for the new bodies.
Add the new bodies to any generator used by the dataset builder (schema knock-on).
Extend with the verified Venus/Sun propagation cases (B.5).

task_c_design_proposal.c3_validation_plan: Re-run the two Task B scripts as regression fixtures after implementing C.2, and add one Mercury-centered and one Jupiter-centered point-mass case to confirm the same point-mass pattern generalizes.

c4_unverified_register.how_to_verify: Query JPL/NASA Horizons or DE405 official GM table; resolve to a cited value.

c4_unverified_register.why: Set-only Mu; source is a codebase constant
c4_unverified_register.how_to_verify: Cite an authoritative reference and/or confirm GMAT's internal default from an external source.
Confirm intended source (GMAT-consistent vs MRO/GM convention) and document the choice.

task_d_physics_sanity.basis: For a circular orbit, v = sqrt(mu / r) with r = SMA. Cross-checked with Task B telemetry.

d1_venus.stability: SMA held 6999.9-7000.0 km; ECC <= ~1.1e-5 -> circular orbit maintained. PASS

d2_sun.match: within 1e-7 (29.78 km/s is Earth's mean heliocentric speed - physically correct at 1 AU)
d2_sun.stability: SMA held 149597870.7 km; ECC <= ~7.7e-16 -> circular heliocentric orbit maintained. PASS

task_d_physics_sanity.d3_au: GMAT/DE405 AU = 149,597,870.691 km default (DE405 readme :377 lists AU = 1.495978706910000e+08); the Sun script used 149597870.7 km (1 AU) and matched the expected 29.7846 km/s speed exactly, confirming internal consistency.

d4_ordering_guards.radius: Sun(695700) > Jupiter(71492) > Earth(6378) > Venus(6051.8) > Mars(3396.19) > Mercury(2440.53) > Moon(1737.4) - consistent; Jupiter radius is ~11.2x Earth's - physically correct.
d4_ordering_guards.mu: Sun(1.33e11) > Jupiter(1.27e8) > Earth(~3.986e5) > Venus(3.249e5) > Mars(4.283e4) > Moon(4.903e3) - physically correct.

summary.task_a: All hard-coded body assumptions are limited to {Earth, Moon, Mars} (constants, schema literals, generator, frontstep, datasets).
summary.task_b: GMAT R2026a verified - DE405 in use; seven-body radii from SPICE TPC; Venus/Mars GM from cof; Sun/Jupiter GM + AU from DE405 readme; Mu/Radius are set-only; planet-centered (Venus) AND heliocentric (Sun) circular propagation both run and hold SMA/ECC; Sun/Mercury/Jupiter have no shipped potential file so must be point masses.
summary.task_c: Design proposal to generalize the central-body table and emit the correct force-model shape per body; not implemented.
summary.task_d: Circular-orbit velocity checks match telemetry to <=4e-6 relative; radius/mu orderings are physically correct.
